condition: Peptic ulcer disease with upper GI bleed
presentingComplaint: Vomiting altered blood and passing black tarry stools for one day
history: One-day history of two episodes of coffee-ground/frank haematemesis followed by three episodes of black, tarry, offensive-smelling melena, with light-headedness on standing. Two-month history of intermittent epigastric burning pain, worse at night and partially relieved by antacids. Regular ibuprofen 400 mg TDS for chronic low-back pain over the past 3 months, no gastroprotection. Ex-smoker, moderate alcohol. No prior GI bleed, no known liver disease, no anticoagulants. No weight loss or dysphagia.
examination: Pale, cool peripheries, mild postural dizziness. Epigastric tenderness without guarding or rebound. Digital rectal examination reveals melena. No stigmata of chronic liver disease (no spider naevi, palmar erythema, ascites or splenomegaly), no jaundice. Chest clear, abdomen soft, bowel sounds present.
imaging: Erect chest X-ray: no free subdiaphragmatic air (excludes perforation). CT not indicated at this stage.
microbiology: H. pylori stool antigen sent; n/a for empiric decision
finalDiagnosis: Bleeding peptic (duodenal) ulcer secondary to NSAID use
citations: Harrison 22e - Peptic Ulcer Disease and Gastrointestinal Bleeding
ACG Upper Gastrointestinal and Ulcer Bleeding 2021
contraindications: Caution with high-dose IV PPI in renal impairment; here creatinine normal
edgeCases: Elevated urea with normal creatinine (raised urea:creatinine ratio) is a clue to upper GI bleed from digested blood, not renal failure
Absence of liver stigmata and normal INR/platelets argues against variceal bleed
A normal Hb early can falsely reassure before haemodilution; trend it
expectedMaiK: Classic NSAID-associated bleeding peptic ulcer presenting as haematemesis and melena with an elevated urea:creatinine ratio and no features of chronic liver disease. Resuscitate, calculate Glasgow-Blatchford score, give IV PPI, and arrange urgent upper GI endoscopy within 24 hours; test and treat H. pylori.
expectedNextQuestions: Detailed NSAID/aspirin/anticoagulant and antiplatelet drug history
Any features of chronic liver disease or prior variceal bleed?
Ongoing haematemesis, syncope, or amount of blood passed?
expectedInvestigations: Urgent upper GI endoscopy (diagnostic and therapeutic) within 24h
